primitives.note: Ionian Fervor: up to 4 stacks of bonus attack speed, each lasting 6s, refreshed by basic attacks/ability hits on enemy champions, large monsters or structures.
At 4 stacks (max), basic attacks deal bonus magic on-hit damage (flat by-level + 20% bonus AD).
Bladesurge deals physical damage on collision with the target or at dash completion.
Irelia is automatically ordered to acquire and attack the Bladesurge target as soon as the dash completes, effectively forcing an immediate basic attack.
Bladesurge's cooldown is fully reset if the target dies to/during the dash, or reduced to 0.2s (a near-reset) if the target was marked Unsteady and is consumed on collision.
E's and R's initial hit apply an 'Unsteady' mark (5s) to the enemy champion hit; Bladesurge (Q) consumes the mark on collision to shorten its own cooldown.
Defiant Dance channels for up to 1.5s (damage ramps over the first 0.75s), granting physical/magic damage reduction; the charge cannot be interrupted by CC but blocks other actions until recast.
Defiant Dance's damage and damage-reduction effect are delivered via a separately-timed recast swipe (manual or automatic) after the channel.
Flawless Duet places two separately-timed blades (initial cast + recast, auto-recast at 3.5s if not manual); damage/stun only occurs once both blades converge.
Vanguard's Edge deals magic damage to enemies hit by the initial projectile barrage on cast (after 0.4s cast time).

The perimeter/zone deals a second instance of magic damage only to enemies that pass through the blade perimeter for the first time; whether a stationary dummy ever 'passes through' this zone is a geometric assumption the dummy fight must make.
Mana costs (Q 15, W 70-90, E 50, R 100) on a champion with no innate mana scaling could meaningfully cap total casts across a 15s fight absent mana items/runes.

needsBespoke.why: Every damage-relevant mechanic (stacking AS + onhit magic bonus on P, dash-collision damage/attack-reset/cooldown-refund on Q, charge-then-recast damage on W, two-part recast-and-converge damage on E, initial-hit-plus-zone damage on R, and the shared Unsteady mark/consume interaction) is expressible as a combination of existing primitives; no unique non-listed mechanic (e.g. resource conversion, stance change, pet) is present.

unsettled.question: Does Vanguard's Edge's perimeter/zone damage (a full second instance of the R base damage + AP ratio) ever land on a stationary target dummy that was already hit by the initial barrage and never moves afterward?
options: The zone never re-damages a target that doesn't move after being hit, so only the initial missile damage should be simulated per R cast
The target's position at the moment of being hit counts as 'passing through' the forming perimeter, so the zone damage should also be applied once per R cast
Neither instance of zone damage should be assumed reliably reproducible in a no-movement dummy fight; treat it as situational/unavailable
quotes: Enemies that pass through the blades for the first time are dealt the same {{as|magic damage}} and are {{tip|slow|slowed}} by 90% for {{fd|1.5}} seconds.
In addition to its {{tip|projectile}}, ''Vanguard's Edge'' will check for enemy champions within a {{tip|cr|icononly=true}} 90-unit radius area from the projectile's origin point.

unsettled.question: What is the actual minimum delay before Flawless Duet can be recast (and thus how quickly the convergence/stun/damage lands after the initial cast)? The wiki states 0.15s, but the bin's IreliaE.CDBetweenCast is 0.25.
options: Use the wiki's stated 0.15s minimum recast delay
These are different mechanics (one governs recast eligibility, the other something else) and both may be simultaneously true
quotes: can be recast after {{fd|0.15}} seconds while the blade is active

unsettled.question: Does the convergence of Flawless Duet's two blades (and thus its damage) take 0.25s (wiki) or 0.35s (bin's IreliaE.RevTime), affecting how much of the 15s window each E cast consumes and thus how many casts fit?
options: Use the wiki's stated 0.25s convergence time
RevTime is an unrelated internal field, not the convergence time at all

unsettled.question: In the maximizing-damage simulation, should Defiant Dance always be charged to the full 0.75s+ ramp before recasting (since the dummy never fights back and there's no risk), or should some shorter/partial charge be modeled to reflect realistic play?
options: Always full-charge to 0.75s+ before recast for maximum swipe damage, since the dummy poses no threat in the damage fight
Model a shorter, more 'realistic' charge time that trades some damage for tempo
Charge time is a free player choice each cast and the simulator should treat it as a build/rotation variable rather than a fixed assumption
quotes: damage increases over the first {{fd|0.75}} seconds of the channel
''Defiant Dance's'' charge cannot be {{tip|interrupt|interrupted}} by {{tip|crowd control}}

proposal: Open with Q (Bladesurge) on the dummy to engage instantly, dealing physical damage, healing, and generating an Ionian Fervor stack, then auto-attack (Q's forced attack-acquire) immediately after.

Cast E (Flawless Duet) targeting the dummy's location right after Q lands (E can be cast during Q's dash), then recast E once the minimum delay has passed so the blades converge on the dummy for magic damage and mark it Unsteady.
Start charging W (Defiant Dance) and hold the channel to its full 0.75s+ ramp (safe, since the dummy never attacks back), then recast the swipe onto the dummy for maximum physical damage.
Cast R (Vanguard's Edge) on cooldown once available, aimed through the dummy, for its initial magic burst damage.
Recast Q on cooldown throughout the fight; because E/R mark the dummy Unsteady, a fresh Q consuming that mark on collision drops its cooldown to ~0.2s, letting it be recast almost immediately.

Fill all remaining time between ability casts with basic attacks on the dummy, both for base auto-attack damage and to keep Ionian Fervor stacked at 4 for its bonus on-hit magic damage, and to refresh the stack duration.
Loop W (charge to max, recast) -> E (cast, recast) -> Q (spam via mark-reset cooldown) -> R (on cooldown) -> auto-attacks in the gaps, for the remaining duration of the 15s fight.
questions: Given Irelia's moderate ability costs (W 70-90, R 100) and no innate mana scaling, will the simulated build's mana pool actually sustain this full-channel, spam-Q rotation for the whole 15s, or does mana become a binding constraint that should change the proposed order/frequency of casts?

Should the simulator assume Q always has a valid target to dash to for every cast within the 15s window (i.e., can Q be recast on the same stationary dummy indefinitely), or does something about Bladesurge's targeting restrict how often it can be re-cast on a single target?

Does the opening order (Q first vs. W first vs. E first) materially change total damage in a 15s window given the differing cooldowns, or is it dominated purely by fitting in the maximum number of each ability's casts regardless of order?

Should Ionian Fervor's on-hit magic bonus be assumed to be active (at 4 stacks) for the majority of the 15s fight, given the opening sequence involves several ability hits on the single target that would build stacks quickly, or is there a meaningful ramp-up period before max stacks that the rotation should account for?
